events.region: Great Salt Lake Desert and Mountains; Northern Wasatch Front
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 313 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Great Salt Lake South of the Causeway, or 24 miles north of
Grantsville, moving north at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Great Salt Lake South of the Causeway and Hat Island.

This storm will be capable of producing strong gusty winds on the
Great Salt Lake. This will lead to a sudden increase in waves and
very choppy waters which will result in hazardous boating conditions.
Boaters are urged to seek safe harbor if possible.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northwestern El Paso County in western Texas...

* WHEN...Until 400 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 312 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Central El Paso, East El Paso, Northeast El Paso, Mission Valley,
Fort Bliss, Biggs Field and Franklin Mountains State Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Western Capes
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...East winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island and Western Capes.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Thursday to 1 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong front moving inland from the eastern
Bering will bring gusty southeasterly winds to the Kuskokwim Delta
coast and the Western Capes beginning Thursday morning. Winds are
expected to peak around noon Thursday, then steadily diminish
through Thursday evening.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...West winds 45 to 65 mph with gusts up to 80 mph expected.

* WHERE...Atka and Adak.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 10 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very strong westerly winds will initiate
Thursday morning due to a deep low pressure system in the southern
Bering Sea. Favored East-West channels could promote locally higher
gusts. Strongest winds are expected from about noon to 3pm AKDT.
Winds to steadily diminish through Thursday night.
